n293f2aa4ef3.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that bandhs are illegal as they curb the freedoms of others?
n293f2aa4ef3.x: CPI(M) v. Bharat Kumar held bandhs illegal because they curb others' freedoms. Kameshwar Prasad protected demonstrations but not strikes, and T.K. Rangarajan denied government employees a right to strike.

n8ca6e0d2362.s: Which case recognised speech and trade over the internet as protected under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g)?
n8ca6e0d2362.x: Anuradha Bhasin protected speech and trade over the internet and required internet shutdowns to be proportionate, temporary and published.

n0788ef98762.s: The right to reside and settle in any part of India is guaranteed by Article:
n0788ef98762.x: Article 19(1)(e) guarantees the right to reside and settle; 19(1)(b) is assembly, 19(1)(d) movement and 19(1)(g) profession, trade or business.

n7ae4654f086.s: The right to silence (not singing the national anthem) was read into Article 19(1)(a) in:
n7ae4654f086.x: Bijoe Emmanuel recognised the right to silence. Tata Press concerned commercial speech, Naveen Jindal flag hoisting and Anuradha Bhasin internet speech.

nc4ec40ff40b.s: Telecast rights and the absence of a government monopoly over airwaves under Article 19(1)(a) are associated with:
nc4ec40ff40b.x: Cricket Association of Bengal concerned telecast and the absence of a government monopoly over airwaves; PUCL is associated with safeguards against phone tapping.

n0a4b2f0e23c.s: The freedoms guaranteed under Article 19 are available to:
o: Citizens and companies as legal persons
n0a4b2f0e23c.x: Article 19 rights are available only to citizens; foreigners cannot claim them and a company as a legal person cannot itself claim them.

nd7ee9fc98b7.s: Reasonable restrictions on the freedom of assembly are provided under Article:
nd7ee9fc98b7.x: Article 19(3) concerns assembly; 19(2) covers speech, 19(5) movement and residence, and 19(6) profession, trade or business.

nindian-polity-16-7.s: Co-operative societies were added to Article 19(1)(c) by which Constitutional Amendment?
nindian-polity-16-7.x: The 97th Amendment (2011) added co-operative societies to Article 19(1)(c). The 44th deleted the Right to Property and the 86th added the Right to Education.

nebdd5375b9f.s: Which ground was added to Article 19(2) by the Sixteenth Amendment, 1963?
nebdd5375b9f.x: Sovereignty and integrity of India came with the Sixteenth Amendment, 1963; the other three grounds were added by the First Amendment, 1951.

nindian-polity-16-16.s: Protection in respect of conviction for offences is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-16-16.x: Article 20 gives protection in respect of conviction; Article 21 protects life and personal liberty, 22 protects against arrest and detention, and 19 lists the six freedoms.

nfafad89aa81.s: The right to acquire, hold and dispose of property, later deleted, was earlier contained in Article:
nfafad89aa81.x: The property right belonged to Article 19(1)(f) and was later deleted; Article 19(1)(c) covers associations, unions and co-operative societies.

n8baba71ae8f.s: Which of the following is a ground for restricting the freedom of assembly under Article 19(3)?
n8baba71ae8f.x: Article 19(3) permits restrictions on assembly in the interests of sovereignty and integrity of India and public order; morality and security of the State are not its grounds.

n2eea285eaee.s: The right to travel abroad is protected under:
n2eea285eaee.x: Travel abroad is protected under Article 21, not under Article 19(1)(d).

n5df8ca76640.s: In India, the right to strike is:
n5df8ca76640.x: The right to strike is not a Fundamental Right; it is only a legal right. A gherao is also not protected as peaceful assembly.

ncb43640c2d6.s: Peaceful protest is recognised as a right of everybody, but a protest ____.
o: may occupy public space without restriction
is a Fundamental Right to strike
ncb43640c2d6.x: Peaceful protest is a right, but it cannot occupy public space without limitation or trouble other citizens.

nindian-society-51-18.s: The statutory Zero FIR is a provision of the:
nindian-society-51-18.x: The statutory Zero FIR is a BNSS provision, not a BNS one; BNS covers organised crime and mob lynching.

n03987baea8b.s: 'General public interest' is a ground for reasonable restrictions under Article:
n03987baea8b.x: General public interest is a ground under Article 19(5) but not under Article 19(2); sedition and economic grounds are not listed in Article 19(2).

n2bf4b480f49.s: Which of the following is excluded from the freedom of peaceful assembly under Article 19(1)(b)?
n2bf4b480f49.x: Meetings, demonstrations and processions are protected when peaceful and unarmed; armed gatherings are excluded.

n682c4603bca.s: Which clause permits the State to carry on a trade to the exclusion of citizens, thereby allowing State monopolies?
n682c4603bca.x: Article 19(6) lets the State prescribe professional or technical qualifications and carry on a trade to the exclusion of citizens.

nd80c02ee40f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Supreme Court rulings on the right to die?
o: P. Rathinam (1994) held Section 309 IPC unconstitutional
Gian Kaur (1996) held there is no right to die and Section 309 IPC is valid
Aruna Shanbaug (2011) held the living will valid
Common Cause (2018) upheld the living will / advance directive
nd80c02ee40f.x: Aruna Shanbaug allowed passive euthanasia under High Court supervision; it was Common Cause (2018) that upheld the living will.

n3e8b24c7a3a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about protection against double jeopardy?
o: Article 20(2) bars prosecution and punishment more than once for the same offence
Article 20(2) also bars departmental proceedings after a criminal conviction for the same act
The protection covers prosecution and punishment by a court or judicial tribunal
Section 337 BNSS replaces Section 300 CrPC as the corresponding provision
n3e8b24c7a3a.x: Article 20(2) covers only prosecution and punishment by a court or judicial tribunal, not departmental proceedings.

n4825346bfeb.s: Which of the following is NOT a change made by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002?
o: Inserted Article 21A for free and compulsory education of children aged 6 to 14
Changed Article 45 to provide early childhood care and education below 6 years
Added Article 51A(k), a duty of parents to provide education to children aged 6 to 14
Deleted the Right to Property from the Fundamental Rights
n4825346bfeb.x: The Right to Property was deleted by the 44th Amendment, 1978. The 86th Amendment changed Articles 21A, 45 and 51A(k).

n75e41a6a706.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the safeguards in Article 22(1) and 22(2)?
o: An arrested person must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours
The 24 hours exclude the time of journey
The safeguards also cover a civil arrest and the deportation of an alien
The safeguards are not available to an enemy alien or a preventive detainee
n75e41a6a706.x: Arrest under court orders, civil arrest and deportation of aliens fall outside these safeguards; Article 22(3) also excludes enemy aliens and preventive detainees.

n6bbdb07222a.s: Which of the following pairs (case – right read into Article 21) is wrongly matched?
o: Shafin Jahan (2018) – Marry a person of choice
Paschim Banga Khet Mazdoor Samity (1996) – Privacy
n6bbdb07222a.x: Paschim Banga Khet Mazdoor Samity concerned emergency medical care; privacy was recognised in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (2017).

nindian-polity-41-8.s: The right to a clean environment and air was read into Article 21 in:
nindian-polity-41-8.x: Subhash Kumar recognised a clean environment; Parmanand Katara gave emergency medical aid, Olga Tellis shelter and livelihood, and Maneka Gandhi travel abroad.

n0b2c31eb03e.s: Under Article 22(7), who may prescribe the maximum period of preventive detention?
n0b2c31eb03e.x: Article 22(7) permits Parliament to prescribe the maximum period of preventive detention; Article 22(5) requires grounds and an opportunity of representation.

n62a94ef8236.s: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 sought to cut the period of preventive detention without an Advisory Board report to:
n62a94ef8236.x: The 44th Amendment cut it from three to two months, but the clause was never notified, so three months still applies under Article 22(4).

nb9521a23645.s: The right to speedy trial was read into Article 21 in:
nb9521a23645.x: Hussainara Khatoon concerned speedy trial; Maneka Gandhi gave fair procedure, M.H. Hoskot free legal aid and Francis Coralie Mullin human dignity.

nacdafb6a13a.s: The RTE Act, 2009 reserves what share of entry-level seats in unaided private schools for children of weaker groups?
nacdafb6a13a.x: The Act provides 25 per cent entry-level seats in unaided private schools for weaker groups; the provision does not apply to minority schools.

n857714796d3.s: Compensation for violation of human rights under Article 21 is associated with:
n857714796d3.x: Nilabati Behera (1993) is associated with compensation for human rights violations; Puttaswamy recognised privacy.

nbf95f3fc97b.s: The expression 'procedure established by law' is associated with the constitution of:
nbf95f3fc97b.x: 'Procedure established by law' is associated with Japan, while 'due process' is associated with the United States.

nf291171540a.s: The protection under Article 20(1) against a heavier penalty than that applicable when the offence was committed applies to:
nf291171540a.x: Article 20(1) applies to criminal laws; it bars conviction and a greater penalty, but does not necessarily bar the trial itself.

n01e7fecefbe.s: The protection under Article 21 is available to:
n01e7fecefbe.x: Article 21 protects citizens and non-citizens and has been read to include dignity, health and protection against solitary confinement.

na663a1ef192.s: Article 21A was inserted into the Constitution by the:
na663a1ef192.x: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A; the RTE Act, 2009 only gives effect to it, since an Act of Parliament cannot add an Article.

n3f86065cce1.s: In which year was the right-to-education case Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka decided?
n3f86065cce1.x: Mohini Jain was decided in 1992, followed by Unnikrishnan in 1993, the 86th Amendment in 2002 and the RTE Act in 2009.

n35cc2efc1c9.s: In which year was the National Security Act enacted?
n35cc2efc1c9.x: The National Security Act came in 1980, after the Preventive Detention Act (1950), MISA (1971) and COFEPOSA (1974).

nc51f33f3bc5.s: In which year did the Supreme Court decide Common Cause, upholding the living will?
nc51f33f3bc5.x: Common Cause was decided in 2018, after P. Rathinam (1994), Gian Kaur (1996) and Aruna Shanbaug (2011).

nindian-society-47-15.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India – Secularism as a basic feature of the Constitution
Abhiram Singh v. C.D. Commachen – Appeals on religion, race, caste, community or language as corrupt practice
Shakti Vahini v. Union of India – Peaceful protest, subject to not occupying public ways indefinitely
Amit Sahni v. Commissioner of Police – Limits on indefinite occupation of public ways by protest
nindian-society-47-15.x: Shakti Vahini protected the right to choose a life partner under Article 21; the limit on protest occupation came from Amit Sahni.

neb916ace771.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Section 295A IPC (deliberate acts meant to outrage religious feelings)?
o: It was struck down in Rev. Stanislaus v. State of MP (1977)
It was upheld on public-order grounds in Ramji Lal Modi v. State of UP
It now corresponds to Section 299 of the BNS, 2023
Stanislaus dealt with propagation and anti-conversion laws
neb916ace771.x: Section 295A was upheld in Ramji Lal Modi; Stanislaus dealt with anti-conversion laws (upholding the Orissa and MP Acts), not Section 295A.

na0f45f3e201.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 25(2)?
o: 25(2)(a) lets the State regulate economic, financial, political or other secular activity associated with religion
25(2)(b) lets the State provide for social welfare and reform
25(2)(b) lets the State throw open Hindu religious institutions of a public character to all classes of Hindus
25(2)(a) lets the State regulate only spiritual beliefs, not secular activities
na0f45f3e201.x: Article 25(2)(a) reaches secular activity associated with religion, not spiritual belief.

n3093e53e327.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Article 24 – Prohibition of employment of children below 14 in hazardous employment
Article 28 – Freedom from taxes for promotion of a particular religion
Article 25 – Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion
Article 26 – Right of a religious denomination to manage its religious affairs
n3093e53e327.x: Freedom from taxes for promoting a particular religion is Article 27; Article 28 concerns religious instruction or worship in certain institutions.

n559c6119a4d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State anti-conversion laws?
o: The Orissa Act, 1967 and the MP Act, 1968 arose from concern over missionary activity
Later amendments widened their scope to conversions to Islam
In Stanislaus v. State of MP (1977), the Supreme Court struck down these laws
Stanislaus held that propagation does not include forcible conversion
n559c6119a4d.x: Stanislaus upheld these laws, holding that the right to propagate does not include forcible conversion.

ncb24c3e22b6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the terms in Article 25(1)?
o: 'Propagate' means the inner freedom to mould one's relation with God
The freedom to follow no religion falls under 'conscience'
Wearing a turban, crucifix or kirpan is an instance of 'profess'
Worship, rituals and ceremonies integral to the religion fall under 'practise'
ncb24c3e22b6.x: Propagate means spreading one's beliefs to others; the inner freedom to mould one's relation with God is conscience.

nc594c91c15e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Article 26 – A religious denomination's right to manage its religious affairs
Article 27 – No compulsory tax for promotion of a particular religion
Article 28(3) – Attendance at religious instruction can be made compulsory in State-aided institutions
Article 28(1) – No religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds
nc594c91c15e.x: Article 28(3) protects freedom from compulsory attendance: no person can be compelled to attend religious instruction without consent.

nac6e6f6708b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 23(2)?
o: The State may impose compulsory service for public purposes
Such service may include military or social service
The State cannot discriminate solely on grounds of religion, race, caste or class in imposing it
The State must pay remuneration in every case of compulsory service
nac6e6f6708b.x: Article 23(2) does not require payment in every case of compulsory public service.

n49bca461fa5.s:
Assertion (A): In a State-recognised or State-aided institution, attendance at religious instruction can be made compulsory.
Reason (R): Under Article 28(3), attendance at religious instruction in such institutions is voluntary, and a minor needs the guardian's consent.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n49bca461fa5.x: Under Article 28(3) no one can be compelled to attend religious instruction in recognised or aided institutions, so A is false while R is true.

nd9c9fb5477a.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
nd9c9fb5477a.s: The rights of religious denominations under Article 26 are subject to:
o: Security of the State and public order
nd9c9fb5477a.x: Article 26 lets a denomination set up institutions and own and administer property, all expressly subject to public order, morality and health.

nf49b0cbeaf3.s: The Essential Religious Practice doctrine is associated with the:
nf49b0cbeaf3.x: Shirur Mutt is associated with the ERP doctrine; Stanislaus concerned conversion, Bijoe Emmanuel the National Anthem and Shayara Bano instant triple talaq.

n4260bdaec3c.s: The 2026 Sabarimala review reference on the Essential Religious Practice doctrine was heard by a nine-judge Bench headed by:
n4260bdaec3c.x: A nine-judge Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant heard the reference; the Centre argued the burden lies on the person challenging a practice.

n9857b09211a.s: Which Article prevents exclusion of a person from electoral rolls on grounds including religion?
n9857b09211a.x: Article 325 prevents exclusion from electoral rolls on grounds including religion; it does not authorise such exclusion.

n8c22e8508c2.x: The explanation to Article 25 includes Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists within 'Hindus'; another explanation deems wearing kirpans part of the profession of Sikhism.

n099aa16f6a6.s: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, which abolishes debt bondage, was enacted in:
n099aa16f6a6.x: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act is of 1976; ITPA is of 1956 and the Child Labour Act of 1986.

n46f2a007d49.s: In the Sabarimala judgment (2018), the exclusion of women of a certain age group was held to be:
o: Protected because Ayyappa devotees are a separate denomination
n46f2a007d49.x: The 4:1 majority of the five-judge Bench held the exclusion was not an ERP and that Ayyappa devotees were not a separate denomination.

n84aeb3f598a.s: The Arya Samaj's call 'Back to the Vedas', seeking to restore a golden past, is an example of:
n84aeb3f598a.x: Revivalism seeks to restore a golden past, as in 'Back to the Vedas'; fundamentalism is a return to literal scripture rejecting plural readings.

nfa65bf1e59f.s: Punjab's Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act provides punishment for sacrilege of up to:
nfa65bf1e59f.x: The Act, which got assent in April 2026, provides for punishment up to life imprisonment; it is challenged in the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

o: Any fee for the secular administration of religious institutions
Use of taxes to support all religions equally
Compelling payment of taxes whose proceeds promote a particular religion
nc2b7238e529.x: Article 27 bars taxes for promoting a particular religion; it does not bar fees, and taxes may support all religions equally.

nae5280c31e6.s: Which case held secularism to be part of the basic structure of the Constitution?
nae5280c31e6.x: S.R. Bommai (1994) recognised secularism as basic structure, inherent even before the 42nd Amendment; Kesavananda Bharati set out the doctrine itself.

nf2cf2355d2d.s: Trafficking is dealt with under which Section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
nf2cf2355d2d.x: Section 143 of the BNS, which replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024, deals with trafficking; victim consent is immaterial.

n72184b4675b.s: Which mutt is the hereditary Dharmakarta of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD)?
n72184b4675b.x: The Sri Swamy Hathiramji Mutt at Tirupati is the hereditary Dharmakarta of the TTD; the AP Endowments Act, 1987 regulates Hindu temples and mutts.

nb22dd1537a8.s: The right under Article 27 is available to:
nb22dd1537a8.x: Article 27, like Articles 25 and 28, is available to all persons; Article 26 is available to religious denominations or any section of them.

n5cefa379290.s: The Essential Religious Practice test was formulated by the Supreme Court in:
n5cefa379290.x: The ERP test was formulated in 1954 to identify practices integral to a religion; the Constitution does not define 'essential'.

n125a69e7596.s: Propagation under Article 25 does not include a right to convert another person, because that would affect the other person's:
n125a69e7596.x: Propagation means spreading one's beliefs; a right to convert another would impinge on that person's freedom of conscience.

nf2db3801176.s: Compulsory service for a public purpose is permitted as an exception under Article:
nf2db3801176.x: Article 23(1) prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and forced labour; Article 23(2) is the exception for compulsory public service without discrimination.

neb28b33c277.s: The freedoms in Article 25(1) are subject to public order, morality, health and:
o: The other provisions of Part III
neb28b33c277.x: Article 25(1) expressly subjects these freedoms to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III.

nf47bcd0c88e.s: In Zoroastrianism, Ahura Mazda refers to:
o: The highest grade of fire temple
nf47bcd0c88e.x: Ahura Mazda is the supreme god of good, while Angra Mainyu is the destructive or evil spirit.

nindian-society-4-6.s: In Zoroastrianism, the Atash Behram is:
o: The highest grade of fire temple
nindian-society-4-6.x: Atash Behram is the highest grade of fire temple; the Zend Avesta is the holy book, Angra Mainyu the evil spirit and Ahura Mazda the supreme god.

n69a8d122ecb.s: The Bhakti movement, which rejected ritualism and caste, spans roughly the:
n69a8d122ecb.x: Bhakti spans the 6th to the 18th century, and its interaction with Sufi traditions built communal harmony and regional literatures.

n479e5adb5c1.s: Which Directive Principles direct the State to ensure that the tender age of children is not abused and that children are protected against exploitation?
n479e5adb5c1.x: Articles 39(e) and 39(f) protect children's tender age from abuse and ensure healthy development with protection against exploitation.

nd5eebe23983.s: Indian secularism is best described as:
o: A state religion with tolerance of other faiths
A strict bar on all state aid to religious institutions
Complete non-interference by the State in religion
No state religion, with positive state intervention for reform
nd5eebe23983.x: India has no state religion and allows positive state intervention for social and religious reform; state aid to religious institutions is not necessarily barred.

nindian-society-4-13.x: Sallekhana is the Jain ritual fast unto death; Kaivalya is liberation, a Tirthankara a spiritual teacher and Ahimsa non-violence.

nf1f664f963a.s: Which of the following hinders religious pluralism?
o: Freedom to practise any religion or none
nf1f664f963a.x: Religious pluralism is the freedom and security to practise any religion or none, resting on freedom of religion and mutual respect; exclusivism hinders it.

nindian-society-4-11.s: In Buddhism, the Tripitaka refers to:
nindian-society-4-11.x: The Tripitaka is the Buddhist sacred texts; the Sangha is the monastic order, the Dhamma the Buddha's teachings and Nirvana liberation.

o: The law of action and consequence
nindian-society-4-27.x: Karma is the law of action and result; Dharma is duty, Samsara the cycle of rebirth and Moksha liberation.

ne0691f90c88.s:
Assertion (A): The LARR Act, 2013 replaced the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
Reason (R): The LARR Act makes Social Impact Assessment mandatory.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ne0691f90c88.x: Both are features of the LARR Act, 2013, but mandatory Social Impact Assessment does not explain why it replaced the 1894 Act.

n3fd824ff514.s: Article 30(1) gives the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice to:
n3fd824ff514.x: Article 30(1) covers all minorities, religious or linguistic; the State may regulate standards but may not take away their minority character.

ncd3fdd42d87.s: The term 'minority' in the Constitution of India is:
ncd3fdd42d87.x: The Constitution uses 'minority' in Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B without defining it; the NCM Act, 1992 also does not define it.

n3c199ac48fe.s: Which Amendment provided that land under personal cultivation could be acquired only on paying market value?
n3c199ac48fe.x: The 17th Amendment required market value for land under personal cultivation; Article 31 itself was deleted by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

ndc840ad3293.s: What is the unit for determining a linguistic minority in India?
ndc840ad3293.x: The State is the unit for determining a linguistic minority; numerical inferiority and non-dominant status are relevant, and the Constitution does not define the term.

ne1a98137a24.s: The Right to Work under Article 41 is a:
ne1a98137a24.x: Article 41 is a Directive Principle, not a Fundamental Right; the right to information, by contrast, is read into Article 19(1)(a).

n248aef544a0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 32 and Article 226?
o: The Supreme Court can issue five writs, whereas High Courts can issue only three
Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right
A High Court under Article 226 can issue writs for 'any other purpose' too
The right under Article 32 can be suspended under Article 359
n248aef544a0.x: Both the Supreme Court and the High Courts can issue all five writs.

n13dccfca009.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 32?
o: Clause (1) makes the right to move the Supreme Court for Part III rights itself a Fundamental Right
Under clause (2), the Supreme Court may issue directions, orders or writs
Under clause (4), the right may be suspended by an ordinary law of Parliament
Clause (4) says the right shall not be suspended except as the Constitution provides
n13dccfca009.x: Article 32(4) says the right cannot be suspended except as the Constitution provides, not by an ordinary law.

n24d89f46f32.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the writ of mandamus?
o: It is not issued to enforce a discretionary duty
As a general rule, it may be issued against a private individual or body
It is not issued to enforce a legislative function
It is not issued to enforce a non-statutory departmental instruction
n24d89f46f32.x: Mandamus is not ordinarily issued against private bodies, nor for discretionary functions, legislative functions or non-statutory instructions.

n13e49f797e4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about prohibition and certiorari?
o: Prohibition is issued while proceedings are pending
Certiorari is generally issued after an order has been passed
Prohibition directs the lower body to stop the proceedings
Certiorari can never be used in relation to a pending proceeding
n13e49f797e4.x: Certiorari is generally post-decision, but it may also be used to transfer a pending case.

nindian-polity-42-13.s: Which of the following pairs (writ – primary target) is wrongly matched?
o: Habeas Corpus – Public authorities and private individuals
Mandamus – Private individuals as a general rule
Prohibition – Judicial and quasi-judicial bodies only
Quo Warranto – Person holding or claiming a substantive public office
nindian-polity-42-13.x: Mandamus lies against public officials, statutory bodies, inferior courts and tribunals, not ordinarily against private individuals.

n46cbbef365b.s: Which provision lets Parliament empower any other court to exercise the Supreme Court's powers under Article 32?
n46cbbef365b.x: Article 32(3) permits Parliament to empower other courts, though no such law has been made; High Courts issue writs under Article 226.

n76f97380580.s: Before 1950, writ jurisdiction was exercised by the High Courts of:
n76f97380580.x: Before 1950 only the Calcutta, Bombay and Madras High Courts had writ jurisdiction; Article 226 now empowers all High Courts.

n1c4ff63febe.s: Article 32A, which barred challenges to State laws under Article 32, was inserted by the:
n1c4ff63febe.x: The 42nd Amendment inserted Article 32A; the 43rd Amendment omitted Articles 32A, 131A, 144A, 226A and 228A.

nd9e03c7e3d5.s: The writ of Quo Warranto lies against the holder of:
o: A substantive public office created by statute or the Constitution
Any office in a private trust
nd9e03c7e3d5.x: Quo Warranto tests a claim to a substantive public office created by statute or the Constitution and may be sought by any interested person.

nindian-polity-38-70.s: Which writ quashes an order already passed by an inferior court?
nindian-polity-38-70.x: Certiorari quashes an order already passed; prohibition prevents an order from being made.

nb2752ccd77d.s: Which writ directs a lower judicial body to stop continuing proceedings in excess of its jurisdiction?
nb2752ccd77d.x: Prohibition prevents continuation of proceedings, while certiorari quashes an order; both check jurisdictional excess by judicial or quasi-judicial bodies.

ne358fd493b4.s: Under epistolary jurisdiction, a prisoner's letter was treated as a writ petition in:
ne358fd493b4.x: Epistolary jurisdiction treats letters or postcards as writ petitions; Sunil Batra, where a prisoner's letter was acted upon, is the example.

n5e1d4fc8a41.s: The writ of Habeas Corpus may be directed against:
o: Both public authorities and private individuals
n5e1d4fc8a41.x: Habeas Corpus lies against public authorities and private individuals for unlawful detention; it does not require release where detention is lawful.

n3e48640b03f.s: Which 1981 case is associated with the development of Public Interest Litigation?
n3e48640b03f.x: S.P. Gupta (1981) is a key PIL case; Justices P.N. Bhagwati and V.R. Krishna Iyer are associated with PIL.

nindian-polity-15-6.s: High Courts have wider writ jurisdiction than the Supreme Court because, under Article 226, they can issue writs for:
o: Legal rights only, not Fundamental Rights
Fundamental Rights only, but against private bodies
nindian-polity-15-6.x: Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights and 'any other purpose', while the Supreme Court under Article 32 acts only for Fundamental Rights.

nindian-polity-42-33.s: The writ remedies exercised by the Supreme Court and High Courts originated as prerogative remedies under:
nindian-polity-42-33.x: The writs come from the prerogative remedies of English common law and are exercised under Articles 32 and 226.

nindian-polity-42-37.s: Prohibition is called a ____ writ because it operates while the lower proceeding is still pending.
nindian-polity-42-37.x: Prohibition is preventive as it acts while the case is pending, while certiorari is curative as it acts after an order is made.

na6b42f733e1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about recent developments on Article 44?
o: In Pavini Shukla v. Union of India (2026), the Supreme Court suggested a UCC to end gender discrimination
Article 44 is enforceable in court like a Fundamental Right
In March 2026 a three-judge Bench considered deferring to Parliament on Article 44
Article 44 is a Directive Principle with no legal force
na6b42f733e1.x: Article 44 is a DPSP with no legal force and is not enforceable like a Fundamental Right.

nf763882800b.s: Which of the following pairs (Article – Directive) is wrongly matched?
o: Article 48 – Agriculture and animal husbandry on scientific lines
Article 49 – Protection of monuments and places of national importance
Article 47 – Prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs
nf763882800b.x: Article 50 directs separation of the judiciary from the executive; international peace and security is Article 51.

nea291441b0b.s: Which of the following pairs (person – description of the Directive Principles) is wrongly matched?
o: K.T. Shah – A cheque on a bank payable at the convenience of the bank
T.T. Krishnamachari – A veritable dustbin of sentiments
Nasiruddin – New Year's resolutions broken on the second of January
Granville Austin – A veritable dustbin of sentiments
nea291441b0b.x: Granville Austin called the Fundamental Rights and DPSPs together the conscience of the Constitution; 'dustbin of sentiments' was T.T. Krishnamachari's phrase.

nindian-polity-19-14.s: Which of the following pairs (Article – Directive) is wrongly matched?
o: Article 46 – Prohibition of the slaughter of cows and calves
Article 47 – Prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs
nindian-polity-19-14.x: Article 46 promotes the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections; the cow-slaughter ban is Article 48.

n39505132885.s: Which of the following was NOT added to the Directive Principles by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976?
o: Article 39A – Equal justice and free legal aid
n39505132885.x: Article 38(2) was added by the 44th Amendment in 1978; the 42nd Amendment added Articles 39A, 43A, 48A and 39(f).

n455b0c66d3a.s: Which of the following pairs (Directive – implementation) is wrongly matched?
o: Articles 39(b) and 39(c) – Land reforms and ceiling laws
n455b0c66d3a.x: Article 40 (village panchayats) was implemented through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, 1992, not the RTE Act.

nindian-polity-19-15.s: Which of the following pairs (Article – Directive) is wrongly matched?
o: Article 45 – Originally, free and compulsory education up to 14 years
Article 48 – Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry
Article 48A – Safeguarding of forests and wildlife
nindian-polity-19-15.x: Article 49 concerns protection of monuments and places of national importance; the Uniform Civil Code is Article 44.

n9c8a7d5d8c4.s: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
n9c8a7d5d8c4.x: The DPSPs are in Part IV (Articles 36–51); they are fundamental in governance but not enforceable by courts.

n629490bc26c.s: The Instrument of Instructions, an antecedent of the Directive Principles, was found under the:
n629490bc26c.x: The Instrument of Instructions under the 1935 Act and the Karachi Resolution (1931) are antecedents of the DPSPs.

n64f58eec506.s: The Ninth Schedule was introduced by the:
n64f58eec506.x: The First Amendment, 1951 introduced the Ninth Schedule and Articles 31A and 31B; the 73rd Amendment dealt with Panchayati Raj.

nindian-polity-19-12.s: Just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief are directed by Article:
nindian-polity-19-12.x: Article 42 covers humane conditions of work and maternity relief; 38 is welfare of the people, 39 livelihood and equal pay, 41 right to work.

n7e0f092f46f.s: The sanction behind the Directive Principles is:
n7e0f092f46f.x: FRs carry a legal sanction enforced by courts, while DPSPs carry a moral and political sanction.

n41b41019dd8.s: MGNREGA, 2005, linked to Article 41, has since been replaced by the:
n41b41019dd8.x: MGNREGA was replaced by the VB-GRAM G Act; a sharp fall in employment under it has revived the right-to-work debate.

n40ee9b2d117.s: The organisation of village panchayats is directed by Article:
n40ee9b2d117.x: Article 40 covers village panchayats; 39A is free legal aid, 43 living wage and cottage industries, and 44 the Uniform Civil Code.

n6988073029a.s: The immediate constitutional model for India's Directive Principles was the Constitution of:
n6988073029a.x: India took the idea from the Irish Constitution of 1937, which had itself copied it from the Spanish Constitution.

n95feb506ba2.s: Which Article, a directive outside Part IV, deals with the development of Hindi?
n95feb506ba2.x: Article 351 covers development of Hindi and Article 335 SC/ST claims to services; both are non-justiciable directives outside Part IV.

nindian-polity-19-8.s: Which of the following Directive Principles is a liberal-intellectual principle rather than a Gandhian one?
nindian-polity-19-8.x: Article 50 (separation of judiciary) is liberal-intellectual; Articles 40, 43B, 46 and 48 are Gandhian.

nindian-polity-20-13.s: A living wage and promotion of cottage industries are directed by Article:
nindian-polity-20-13.x: Article 43 covers living wage and cottage industries; 39A is free legal aid, 41 right to work and 42 humane work conditions.

n815fd01c290.s: Which Article provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?
n815fd01c290.x: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is under Article 350B; Article 350A concerns mother-tongue education.

ncd10e0bdc37.s: Equal pay for equal work for men and women is provided in Article:
ncd10e0bdc37.x: Article 39(d) deals with equal pay; 39(e) protects the health and strength of workers and children from unsuited work.

n0afc721b082.s: The Legal Services Authorities Act, which implements Article 39A, came into force on 9 November of which year?
n0afc721b082.x: The Act of 1987 came into force on 9 November 1995, observed as National Legal Services Day; it sets up NALSA, SLSAs and DLSAs.

n619521a96ba.s: Which group is exempted from the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026?
n619521a96ba.x: Scheduled Tribes are exempted. Gujarat is the second State after Uttarakhand to move a UCC, providing for monogamy and equal inheritance.

n26a27824e07.s: Who described the Directive Principles as 'a manifesto of aims and aspirations'?
n26a27824e07.x: K.C. Wheare called them a manifesto of aims and aspirations; Ivor Jennings called them 'pious aspirations' and T.T. Krishnamachari 'a veritable dustbin of sentiments'.

o: Free and compulsory education up to fourteen years
Early childhood care and education until six years
nc146f9b9d58.x: Article 45 now covers early childhood care and education until age six; education for ages 6–14 is a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.

n0dc146946cb.s: Which of the following Directive Principles is grouped under the Gandhian, not the Socialist, principles?
n0dc146946cb.x: Article 43B (co-operative societies) is Gandhian; Articles 38, 39A and 47 are generally grouped under Socialist principles.

n978dccaa78f.s: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 support which Directive Principle?
n978dccaa78f.x: Article 48A is supported by wildlife and environmental legislation; Article 47 is reflected in public health measures such as the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017.

n1a8aa7989eb.s: Article 38(2) of the Directive Principles was added by the:
n1a8aa7989eb.x: Article 38(2) was added by the 44th Amendment in 1978; Article 43B came by the 97th (2011) and the present Article 45 by the 86th (2002).

n1c9b9a6ac04.s: Heritage and monuments are covered by Article 49 and by Fundamental Duty:
n1c9b9a6ac04.x: Article 49 and Article 51A(f) relate to heritage; Article 45 pairs with 51A(k) on education, and Article 39 with 51A(e) on women's dignity.

nindian-polity-20-6.s: The Directive Principles of State Policy aim to establish:
o: Social and economic democracy and a welfare state
nindian-polity-20-6.x: The DPSPs aim at social democracy, economic democracy and a welfare state; the idea was borrowed from Ireland.

n0fe144ea9e7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the judicial history of Article 39(b)?
o: In Ranganatha Reddy (1977), Justice Krishna Iyer's minority view included privately owned resources in 'material resources of the community'
Property Owners Association held that every privately owned resource automatically falls within Article 39(b)
The broad view was followed in Sanjeev Coke (1983)
Property Owners Association was decided in 2024
n0fe144ea9e7.x: The 2024 Property Owners Association decision rejected the proposition that every privately owned resource automatically falls within Article 39(b).

n9a49761de66.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 31C?
o: It was introduced by the 25th Amendment in 1971
It protects laws giving effect to Articles 39(b) and 39(c)
Articles 39(b) and 39(c) are the only Directive Principles that override Fundamental Rights under it
Minerva Mills upheld the 42nd Amendment's extension of it to all Directive Principles
n9a49761de66.x: Minerva Mills struck down the 42nd Amendment's extension of Article 31C protection to all Directive Principles.

n49b914ba570.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951)?
o: It held that Fundamental Rights prevail and DPSPs run subsidiary to them
It struck down a Madras communal order on admissions under Article 29(2)
It adopted harmonious construction under which DPSPs prevail over Fundamental Rights
It led to the insertion of Article 15(4)
n49b914ba570.x: Harmonious construction came in In re Kerala Education Bill (1958), and even there Fundamental Rights still prevail.

nc1a705967a7.s:
Assertion (A): Article 48A read with Article 21 has been used to support the right to a healthy environment.
Reason (R): Directive Principles are entirely excluded from constitutional interpretation because they are non-justiciable.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nc1a705967a7.x: Courts use Directive Principles to enrich Fundamental Rights (e.g. Article 48A with 21, Article 45 with 21); non-justiciability does not exclude them from interpretation.

n9726c2de193.s: In Waman Rao (1981), laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after which date were held open to challenge?
n9726c2de193.x: Waman Rao used 24 April 1973, the date of the Kesavananda judgment, as the cut-off; I.R. Coelho (2007) rejected blanket immunity.

n5e7fc6d2646.s: Which was the first case of conflict between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles?
n5e7fc6d2646.x: Champakam Dorairajan (1951) was the first conflict case; I.R. Coelho (2007) was the last word on the Ninth Schedule.

n525bcb69410.s: The original Article 31C protected laws giving effect to Articles 39(b) and 39(c) from challenge under Articles:
n525bcb69410.x: The original Article 31C shielded such laws from Articles 14, 19 and 31, and put the declaration that they implemented the policy beyond judicial question.

nindian-polity-15-22.s: Which 1950 case gave a narrow interpretation of Article 21?
o: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
nindian-polity-15-22.x: A.K. Gopalan (1950) read Article 21 narrowly; Golaknath (1967) barred amendment of FRs and Kesavananda (1973) protected the basic structure.

n06154e6b527.s: Which case denied Parliament the power to amend Fundamental Rights and applied the doctrine of prospective overruling?
n06154e6b527.x: Golaknath (1967) gave FRs a 'transcendental' position and applied prospective overruling; 'amendable but not the Basic Structure' is Kesavananda Bharati.

n4b466524a92.s: Which Amendment attempted to extend Article 31C protection to laws implementing all the Directive Principles?
n4b466524a92.x: The 42nd Amendment, not the 44th, attempted the extension, and it was struck down by the Supreme Court.

nf95a3b6c15e.s: Article 15(4), inserted by the First Amendment Act, 1951, was a response to which judgment?
nf95a3b6c15e.x: Article 15(4) answered Champakam Dorairajan; Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule answered the land-reform judgments.

na7dfcab71f0.s: Fundamental Rights are mostly ____, while Directive Principles are positive directions to the State.
na7dfcab71f0.x: FRs are mostly negative and aim at political democracy; DPSPs are positive and aim at social and economic democracy.

nd6e0e21ff96.s: Article 31C was inserted into the Constitution by the:
nd6e0e21ff96.x: Article 31C came with the Twenty-fifth Amendment; the Seventeenth widened 'estate' in Article 31A and dealt with land under personal cultivation.

n288b5f1f75b.s: The 7:2 majority opinion in Property Owners Association v. State of Maharashtra (2024) was written by:
n288b5f1f75b.x: CJI D.Y. Chandrachud wrote the nine-judge Bench's majority; it rejected Justice Krishna Iyer's 1977 Ranganatha Reddy minority view.

nindian-polity-51-14.s: The First Constitutional Amendment Act, which added Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule, was enacted in:
nindian-polity-51-14.x: The 1st Amendment (1951) added Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule to protect land-reform and welfare laws from early court rulings.

n89096352804.s: In which year was Minerva Mills decided?
n89096352804.x: Minerva Mills (1980) came after Kesavananda Bharati (1973) and before Sanjeev Coke (1983).

na62a866d728.s: In which year was I.R. Coelho, the last word on the Ninth Schedule, decided?
na62a866d728.x: I.R. Coelho came in 2007, after Champakam Dorairajan and the First Amendment (1951) and Minerva Mills.

nb1f01804005.s:
Assertion (A): The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 relates to the Fundamental Duty to protect the sovereignty and integrity of India.
Reason (R): The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 relates to promotion of harmony and prevention of caste or religious offences.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nb1f01804005.x: Both statements correctly link a law to a Fundamental Duty, but the Civil Rights Act's link to harmony does not explain the UAPA's link to sovereignty.

nindian-polity-18-7.s: Which clause of Article 51A asks citizens to cherish the noble ideals that inspired the freedom struggle?
nindian-polity-18-7.x: Clause (b) covers the ideals of the freedom struggle; (a) respect for Constitution, Flag and Anthem, (c) sovereignty and integrity, (d) defence of the country.

n9f88a8c1788.s: Article 48A, relating to the environment, is a:
o: Directive Principle addressed to the State
n9f88a8c1788.x: Article 48A is a Directive Principle addressed to the State; the citizens' duty is in Article 51A(g), and Article 21 is read to include a clean environment.

n7eff2c08c56.s: Which Fundamental Duty is specifically addressed to parents or guardians?
n7eff2c08c56.x: Only Article 51A(k) addresses parents or guardians; clauses (b), (f), (h) and (j) are generally regarded as moral duties.

nindian-polity-18-4.s: Developing scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A clause:
nindian-polity-18-4.x: Clause (h) is scientific temper; (e) is harmony and dignity of women, (f) composite culture and (g) the natural environment.

n29dd29a52eb.s: Environmental protection appears in the Directive Principle Article 48A and in Fundamental Duty:
n29dd29a52eb.x: Environment is in Article 48A and 51A(g); education links Article 45, 21A and 51A(k); heritage links Article 49 and 51A(f).

nd0214c2ff52.s: In M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India, CSR including environmental protection was linked to:
nd0214c2ff52.x: The case held that CSR includes environmental protection and linked the principle to the Fundamental Duty in Article 51A(g).

n493e2bdab7f.s: Renouncing practices derogatory to the dignity of women is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A clause:
n493e2bdab7f.x: Article 51A(e) covers harmony, common brotherhood and renouncing practices derogatory to women; 51A(d) covers defending the country.

nfe3fcd8d9a7.s: Which case held that Fundamental Duties cannot override Fundamental Rights and that respect for national symbols does not require compelled participation?
o: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala
nfe3fcd8d9a7.x: In Bijoe Emmanuel (1986), the Court held Fundamental Duties cannot override Part III rights and respect for symbols needs no compelled participation.

n1a4ba3ce922.s: Which Fundamental Duty proposed by the Swaran Singh Committee was not included in the Constitution?
n1a4ba3ce922.x: The committee suggested payment of taxes as a Fundamental Duty, but the proposal was not accepted.

nd3d688848a1.s: The Fundamental Duties are contained in which Part, one of the four Parts added to the Constitution after 1950?
nd3d688848a1.x: Fundamental Duties are in Part IVA; Parts IVA, IXA, IXB and XIVA are the four Parts added after 1950.

nindian-polity-21-24.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about presidential action on Bills?
o: The President may withhold assent to an Ordinary Bill
The President may return an Ordinary Bill once
The President may return a Money Bill once for reconsideration
The President may withhold assent to a Money Bill
nindian-polity-21-24.x: A Money Bill can be assented to or withheld but never returned; only an ordinary Bill can be returned once.

nindian-polity-21-33.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the passage of Bills?
o: A Financial Bill (I) can only be recommended on, not rejected or amended, by the Rajya Sabha
An Ordinary Bill may originate in either House, with equal powers for the Rajya Sabha
A Money Bill originates only in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha may only make recommendations
A Constitution Amendment Bill may originate in either House and must pass each House separately
nindian-polity-21-33.x: A Financial Bill (I) originates only in the Lok Sabha, but the Rajya Sabha has full power to reject or amend it.

n195d712c8b3.s: Which of the following can NOT be changed by Parliament by a simple majority outside Article 368?
o: Formation of new States and alteration of their boundaries
The basic structure of the Constitution
Creation or abolition of Legislative Councils in States
Change in the official language under Article 343
n195d712c8b3.x: The basic structure cannot be amended even by the special procedure; the other three are simple-majority matters outside Article 368.

nfe7f719f672.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the constitutional amendment procedure?
o: Parliament alone can amend most provisions
No outside convention or special body is required
Ratification by the States is required for every amendment
States cannot initiate an amendment under Article 368
nfe7f719f672.x: State ratification is required only for a limited group of federal provisions, not for every amendment.

n86010077b43.s:
Assertion (A): The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 inserted clauses (4) and (5) in Article 368.
Reason (R): Through these clauses the 42nd Amendment sought to declare the amending power unlimited and to bar judicial review of constitutional amendments.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n86010077b43.x: The 42nd Amendment inserted clauses (4) and (5) precisely to declare the amending power unlimited and bar judicial review of amendments.

nindian-polity-67-12.s: Which case(s) held that constitutional amendments are not 'law' under Article 13(2)?
nindian-polity-67-12.x: Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh held so; Golaknath barred abridging FRs, Kesavananda allowed amendment within the basic structure, and Minerva Mills held limited amending power basic.

n0041f387500.s: Creation or abolition of a State Legislative Council under Article 169 requires:
o: A simple majority of Parliament, outside Article 368
A special majority plus ratification by half of the States
A special majority of the State Legislature only
n0041f387500.x: Legislative Councils are dealt with by simple majority outside Article 368; the President's election needs special majority plus State ratification.

nindian-polity-21-12.s: A Constitution Amendment Bill must be passed by a special majority in:
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
The Lok Sabha, with recommendations from the Rajya Sabha
nindian-polity-21-12.x: An amendment Bill can start in either House without the President's recommendation and needs a special majority in each House separately; there is no joint sitting.

n88ba159f901.s: Which case first applied the basic-structure doctrine?
n88ba159f901.x: Kesavananda Bharati first propounded the doctrine and Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain first applied it; Golaknath first limited the amending power over FRs.

n81893dddc5d.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposed raising the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to:
n81893dddc5d.x: It sought 850 seats with delimitation but failed in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026 (298 for, short of the 352 needed); there is no joint sitting for amendment Bills.

n61bff1f62c6.s: Which of the following can be changed by Parliament by a simple majority outside Article 368?
n61bff1f62c6.x: Quorum, MPs' salaries and parliamentary privileges are simple-majority matters outside Article 368; the others need a special majority.

n7b2ce984996.s: Which of the following requires a special majority of Parliament along with ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures?
n7b2ce984996.x: The Seventh Schedule, the President's election and representation of States need State ratification; Fundamental Rights need only a special majority.

nf6ad1caf0e7.s: The amendment procedure of the Constitution of India is:
o: Wholly flexible, with every provision amendable by simple majority
A combination of rigidity and flexibility
nf6ad1caf0e7.x: The procedure combines rigidity and flexibility, and the basic-structure limitation permits judicial review of amendments.

neb94fcbdb15.s: Changes relating to Articles 2, 3 and 169 of the Constitution can be made by:
o: A special majority plus ratification by half the States
A simple majority, without being deemed amendments under Article 368
neb94fcbdb15.x: Changes under Articles 2, 3 and 169 are made by simple majority and are not deemed amendments under Article 368; the Constitution has both flexible and rigid methods.

nbb03dbb32ba.s: The Kesavananda Bharati judgment upheld which Constitutional Amendment?
nbb03dbb32ba.x: Kesavananda Bharati upheld the 24th Amendment and held that FRs and the Preamble are amendable but the basic structure cannot be altered.

n08ca829b75b.s: If either House of Parliament rejects a Constitutional Amendment Bill:
o: A joint sitting is summoned to resolve it
n08ca829b75b.x: There is no joint sitting for a Constitutional Amendment Bill, so rejection by either House causes failure; once duly passed, assent is obligatory under the 24th Amendment.

nd444aa1ee89.s: What time limit is prescribed for State ratification of an amendment affecting specified federal provisions?
nd444aa1ee89.x: State ratification is needed only for specified federal provisions, not every amendment, and no time limit is prescribed for it.

o: A special majority plus ratification by half the States
A special majority of Parliament without State ratification
No procedure, as it cannot be amended at all
n8edc0e72267.x: Article 32 may be amended by special majority without State ratification, though the Supreme Court's power under it is part of the basic structure.

n0ea64af1ceb.s: A Bill for amendment of the Constitution may be introduced:
o: By a minister or a private member, without the President's prior permission
Only by a minister, with the President's prior permission
Only after ratification by the States
n0ea64af1ceb.x: An amendment Bill needs no prior presidential permission and may be moved by a private member; Article 108 joint sittings do not apply to it.

nindian-polity-23-6.s: Amendments to specified federal provisions require ratification by:
o: At least one-half of the State Legislatures
nindian-polity-23-6.x: Federal provisions need ratification by at least half the States; the President's qualifications and tenure need no ratification.

nindian-polity-21-15.s: In case of a deadlock between the two Houses over an Ordinary Bill, the Constitution provides for:
o: A final decision by the President
Passage by the Lok Sabha alone
nindian-polity-21-15.x: An ordinary Bill needs a simple majority, both Houses have equal powers over it, and a deadlock can go to a joint sitting.

nindian-polity-23-32.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: 91st Amendment (2003) – Barred defectors from ministerial posts (Articles 75(1A) and 164(1A))
97th Amendment (2011) – Part IX-B, permitting a maximum of 31 directors under Article 243ZJ
101st Amendment (2016) – GST and the GST Council under Article 279A
nindian-polity-23-32.x: Article 243ZJ, added by the 97th Amendment, permits a maximum of 21 directors, not 31.

nindian-polity-23-27.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the 73rd Amendment?
nindian-polity-23-27.x: Constitutional status to Municipalities came with the 74th Amendment; the other three belong to the 73rd.

n2980b801e9b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the rulings overcome by the First Amendment?
o: Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar concerned zamindari abolition / land reform
Romesh Thappar (1950) concerned freedom of speech
Articles 31A and 31B were the direct response to Champakam Dorairajan
Champakam Dorairajan concerned a communal order in admissions, leading to Article 15(4)
n2980b801e9b.x: Champakam Dorairajan led to Article 15(4); Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule answered the land-reform judgments.

nd4e7dddef78.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Emergency safeguards of the 44th Amendment Act, 1978?
o: A National Emergency can be proclaimed only on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet
'Armed rebellion' replaced 'internal disturbance' as a ground
The Proclamation must be approved by Parliament within one month
Rights under Articles 20 and 21 can be suspended during an Emergency by Presidential order
nd4e7dddef78.x: After the 44th Amendment, Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during an Emergency.

nindian-polity-43-28.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: 86th Amendment – Right to Education for children aged 6–14
91st Amendment – 15% cap on the Council of Ministers
nindian-polity-43-28.x: The 106th Amendment provides one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies; EWS reservation came with the 103rd.

nindian-polity-23-20.s: Which provision added by the First Amendment, 1951 validates Acts placed in the Ninth Schedule?
nindian-polity-23-20.x: Article 31B validates Ninth Schedule Acts; Article 31A saves estate-acquisition laws and Article 15(4) permits special provisions for backward classes, SCs and STs.

n51c287a0b2d.s: Anti-defection provisions were introduced for the first time by the:
n51c287a0b2d.x: The 52nd Amendment introduced anti-defection provisions; the 91st later modified them.

nindian-polity-23-24.s: Part XIV-A, added by the 42nd Amendment, deals with:
nindian-polity-23-24.x: The 42nd Amendment added Part XIV-A on tribunals, listed Fundamental Duties in Article 51A and shifted education to the Concurrent List.

nindian-polity-23-28.s: The 12th Schedule, added by the 74th Amendment, contains how many subjects?
nindian-polity-23-28.x: The 74th Amendment (1992) added Part IX-A and the 12th Schedule with 18 subjects; the 11th Schedule of the 73rd has 29.

n6b40b503480.s: Which of the following was transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment?
n6b40b503480.x: The 42nd Amendment moved education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice to the Concurrent List.

n9056052c547.s: The delimitation freeze was extended up to 2026 by which Amendment?
n9056052c547.x: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze to 2026; the issue is now linked to the 2027 Census, and the 131st Bill failed in April 2026.

nindian-polity-23-9.s: Privy purses were abolished by the:
nindian-polity-23-9.x: The 26th abolished privy purses; the 24th made presidential assent compulsory, the 44th removed property from FRs and the 52nd added anti-defection law.

n78a00dd6e79.s: Articles 239AA and 239AB, providing Delhi's special constitutional framework, were inserted by the:
n78a00dd6e79.x: The 69th Amendment gave Delhi its framework; the 52nd introduced the Tenth Schedule and the 86th inserted Article 21A.

n1426054c0c8.s: Which Amendment enabled a National Emergency to be proclaimed in only a part of India?
n1426054c0c8.x: The 42nd Amendment enabled Emergency in a part of India; it also inserted Part IVA (Fundamental Duties) and Part XIVA (tribunals).

n15fc3c7cb3a.x: The 24th Amendment inserted Article 13(4), clarified Parliament's power to amend FRs and made presidential assent to amendment Bills obligatory.

n7dbb6c6d1f2.s: Which Amendment made Sikkim a full State?
n7dbb6c6d1f2.x: The 36th (1975) made Sikkim a full State; the 13th (1962) dealt with Nagaland and the 55th (1986) gave Arunachal Pradesh statehood.

nindian-polity-23-33.s: The National Judicial Appointments Commission was created by which Amendment?
nindian-polity-23-33.x: The 99th Amendment (2014) created the NJAC, which the Supreme Court struck down in 2015 for violating judicial independence.

nindian-polity-23-37.s: Which Amendment gave the President one opportunity to return the advice of the Council of Ministers for reconsideration?
nindian-polity-23-37.x: The 42nd Amendment made ministerial advice binding; the 44th let the President return it once.

nindian-polity-23-11.s: Which Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as a ground for National Emergency?
nindian-polity-23-11.x: The 44th Amendment made this change and also let the President return ministerial advice once.

nindian-polity-22-8.s: Which Constitutional Amendment is known as the 'Mini-Constitution'?
nindian-polity-22-8.x: The 42nd Amendment made sweeping changes, such as adding Fundamental Duties and 'Socialist, Secular and Integrity' to the Preamble.

nbcbc5ac11bc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 106th Constitutional Amendment?
o: It has been criticised for not providing a separate sub-quota for BC women
Southern States fear their share may decline after delimitation
It has already been implemented in all State Legislative Assemblies
It provides one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies
nbcbc5ac11bc.x: The women's quota under the 106th Amendment remains unimplemented.

n5ef9a9f4d68.s: In which case did the Supreme Court strike down Part IXB insofar as it applied to State co-operative societies?
o: Union of India v. Rajendra N. Shah (2021)
n5ef9a9f4d68.x: In Rajendra N. Shah (2021), Part IXB (Articles 243ZH–243ZT, added by the 97th Amendment) was struck down for State co-operatives as State ratification was absent.

n90fb2a04865.s: Implementation of the women's reservation under the 2023 law has been linked to the completion of:
n90fb2a04865.x: The women's reservation remains unimplemented because its implementation is linked to the completion of delimitation.

n4d44153c900.s: Under the constitutional provisions on co-operative societies, the term of the board is:
n4d44153c900.x: The board has a five-year term; the provisions also fix a maximum of 21 directors, one SC/ST seat, two women seats and audit within six months.

n433d5e00c23.s: Since 1992, one-third reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities has been provided under Articles:
n433d5e00c23.x: Articles 243D and 243T deal with reservation in Panchayats and Municipalities respectively, giving women one-third seats since 1992.

n6bb40a197c0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Golaknath case (1967)?
o: It held that Fundamental Rights are 'transcendental and immutable'
It was decided by an 11-judge Bench by a 6:5 majority
It arose from a challenge to the 24th Amendment
It held that a constitutional amendment is 'law' under Article 13
n6bb40a197c0.x: Golaknath challenged the 17th Amendment, not the 24th.

n63459f0b82c.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the First Amendment Act, 1951?
o: Addition of public order, friendly relations with foreign States and incitement as grounds under Article 19(2)
n63459f0b82c.x: Article 31C was inserted by the Twenty-Fifth Amendment Act, 1971.

ned440a9f440.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about secularism and the basic structure?
o: Secularism was recognised as a basic feature even before the word was put in the Preamble
Secularism became a basic feature only because of its textual insertion in 1976
The word 'secular' was inserted into the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976
S.R. Bommai held secularism to be part of the basic structure
ned440a9f440.x: Secularism was treated as a basic feature even before the 42nd Amendment added the word 'secular' to the Preamble.

nbe007e991b8.s: Which of the following pairs (basic feature – case) is correctly matched?
o: Rule of law – Delhi Judicial Service Association case
Independence of judiciary – P. Sambamurthy case
nbe007e991b8.x: Bhim Singhji is associated with the welfare state; rule of law goes with P. Sambamurthy, Articles 32, 136, 141 and 142 with Delhi Judicial Service Association, and judicial independence with NJAC.

n36c255c2e01.s: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are:
o: Open to review on the basis of the basic structure
n36c255c2e01.x: Waman Rao used 24 April 1973 as the cut-off; post-cut-off entries are open to basic-structure review rather than enjoying immunity.

nc5fe32b98f7.s: A law can be placed in the Ninth Schedule only by:
o: A State Legislature by ordinary law
nc5fe32b98f7.x: Inclusion needs a constitutional amendment by Parliament; the Schedule covers Central and State laws and was created mainly for land-reform laws.

nc68f4ff7570.x: The doctrine is not expressly defined in the Constitution; it was developed by the Supreme Court and its content has evolved through case law.

nab590e88653.s: The Supreme Court struck down the 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act in 2015 by a majority of:
nab590e88653.x: The NJAC case was decided 4:1, treating judicial independence as part of the basic structure.

n8de89b726e0.s: Which of the following best describes the present position on the Preamble?
o: It is not a part of the Constitution
It is part of the Constitution and amendable, subject to the basic structure
It is part of the Constitution but cannot be amended at all
It alone constitutes the basic structure
n8de89b726e0.x: The Preamble is part of the Constitution and amendable subject to the basic structure doctrine, which is not confined to the Preamble.

n92656eb5c25.s: Which case first propounded the basic structure doctrine and overruled Golaknath?
n92656eb5c25.x: Kesavananda Bharati propounded the doctrine, overruled Golaknath and upheld the 24th Amendment.

n94a54a5c9c0.s: In which year was the Waman Rao judgment on the Ninth Schedule delivered?
n94a54a5c9c0.x: Waman Rao came in 1981, after the First Amendment (1951) and Kesavananda Bharati (1973), and before I.R. Coelho (2007).

nindian-polity-24-46.s: Which of the following pairs (case – linked provision) is wrongly matched?
o: Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillu – 52nd Amendment and Tenth Schedule
Minerva Mills v. Union of India – 39th Constitutional Amendment
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India – Article 356
P. Sambamurthy v. State of A.P. – 32nd Constitutional Amendment
nindian-polity-24-46.x: Minerva Mills is linked to the 42nd Amendment; the 39th Amendment is linked to Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain.

nindian-polity-24-11.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about cases on the Preamble?
o: The Berubari Union case held that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution
Kesavananda Bharati held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution
S.R. Bommai held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution
Golaknath was about the amending power
nindian-polity-24-11.x: Berubari held the opposite, that the Preamble is not part of the Constitution.

nindian-polity-24-4.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: A.K. Gopalan – Preventive detention and procedure established by law
Champakam Dorairajan – Fundamental Rights prevailing over DPSPs
P. Sambamurthy – 52nd Amendment and the Tenth Schedule
Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain – Judicial scrutiny of high constitutional elections
nindian-polity-24-4.x: P. Sambamurthy concerned judicial review and special provisions for Andhra Pradesh; the Tenth Schedule case is Kihoto Hollohan.

n6e93e615dd5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the selection of the CEC and Election Commissioners?
o: Anoop Baranwal (2023) provided for a committee of the PM, the Leader of Opposition and the CJI
The Anoop Baranwal arrangement was permanent and could not be changed by Parliament
Parliament's 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union Minister in the committee
The Court's committee was to operate only till Parliament made a law
n6e93e615dd5.x: The Court's committee was to operate only until Parliament made a law, which Parliament did in 2023.

nc3af4b70bcd.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about judgments on Andhra Pradesh reservation matters?
o: E.V. Chinnaiah (2004) struck down AP's SC sub-categorisation Act, 2000
E.V. Chinnaiah was overruled by State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024)
Chebrolu Leela Prasad Rao (2020) upheld a 100% ST quota for teachers in Scheduled Areas
Chebrolu Leela Prasad Rao was decided in 2020
nc3af4b70bcd.x: Chebrolu Leela Prasad Rao struck down, not upheld, the 100% ST quota for teachers in Scheduled Areas.

n4c7acfd54be.s: Under the Aadhaar judgment, Aadhaar was held NOT mandatory for:
n4c7acfd54be.x: The judgment held Aadhaar not mandatory for bank accounts, SIM cards or school admissions, and did not permit unrestricted data-sharing contracts with private corporations.

n27a55480891.s: Which case made President's Rule under Article 356 subject to judicial review and emphasised the floor test?
n27a55480891.x: The nine-judge S.R. Bommai judgment made Article 356 reviewable, stressed the floor test and recognised secularism as basic structure.

nindian-polity-41-17.s: Guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace were laid down in:
nindian-polity-41-17.x: Vishaka laid down the guidelines; Kihoto Hollohan made Speaker's defection rulings reviewable and Minerva Mills balanced Parts III and IV.

nca4f1524970.s: In Supriyo v. Union of India (October 2023), the issue of same-sex marriage was:
nca4f1524970.x: Supriyo held there is no fundamental right to marry and left same-sex marriage to Parliament; transgender persons in heterosexual relationships can marry under existing law.

n39c6baa6b73.s: Which case held that polygamy is not an essential religious practice?
n39c6baa6b73.x: Javed (2003) held polygamy not an essential religious practice; the SC has issued notice on a PIL to ban polygamy, and bigamy is an offence under Section 82 BNS.

nindian-polity-24-10.s: Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain is linked to which Constitutional Amendment?
nindian-polity-24-10.x: Raj Narain concerned the 39th Amendment; Sambamurthy the 32nd, Kihoto Hollohan the 52nd and Champakam led to the 1st.

nindian-polity-41-22.s: The Berubari Union case dealt with:
nindian-polity-41-22.x: Berubari dealt with Article 3 and the Preamble; Shankari Prasad weighed Article 13 against 368, Raj Narain the 39th and Minerva Mills the 42nd.

n25b385fa378.s: Which 2018 judgment struck down Section 497 of the IPC dealing with adultery?
n25b385fa378.x: Joseph Shine (2018) struck down Section 497 IPC; the BNS, in force from 1 July 2024, has no adultery offence and no Section 377 equivalent.

n89e32462c30.s: Which case made registration of an FIR mandatory for cognizable offences?
n89e32462c30.x: Lalita Kumari made FIR registration mandatory under Section 154 CrPC (now Section 173 BNSS); arrest memos and medical checks are D.K. Basu guidelines.

n6f4b0f3c76f.s: In Union of India v. ADR (2002), the Supreme Court required election candidates to disclose:
o: Criminal record, assets and educational qualifications
n6f4b0f3c76f.x: The ADR judgment required disclosure of criminal record, assets and educational qualifications.

n6d627e8c3ab.s: Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act was struck down in:
n6d627e8c3ab.x: Lily Thomas (2013) concerned disqualification of convicted legislators; Sarla Mudgal and Lily Thomas (2000) dealt with conversion and bigamy.

n5a8f2259456.s: In the December 2023 Article 370 judgment, the Supreme Court treated Article 370 as:
o: Inoperable except by a constitutional amendment
n5a8f2259456.x: The Court treated Article 370 as temporary, upheld the President's power to make it inoperative and directed elections.

n2e8052921a8.s: The nine-judge Puttaswamy (privacy) Bench was associated with which Chief Justice?
n2e8052921a8.x: Puttaswamy was a nine-judge case associated with CJI J.S. Khehar; Bommai was also nine judges, while Maneka Gandhi and Davinder Singh were seven.

nindian-polity-24-29.s: In which year was the Berubari Union case decided?
nindian-polity-24-29.x: Berubari was 1960, after A.K. Gopalan (1950) and Shankari Prasad (1951) and before Sajjan Singh (1965).

nindian-polity-41-45.s: Which case struck down the IMDT Act for breaching the Union's duty under Article 355?
nindian-polity-41-45.x: In Sarbananda Sonowal (2005), the IMDT Act was held to hamper detection of illegal migrants, breaching Article 355.

nindian-polity-41-3.s: The Champakam Dorairajan case led to which Constitutional Amendment?
nindian-polity-41-3.x: Champakam held that FRs prevail over DPSPs, striking down caste-based quotas, so Parliament passed the 1st Amendment adding Article 15(4).

n1fbab16b296.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 254(2)?
o: A State law on a Concurrent List matter may prevail in that State if it receives the President's assent
Parliament may subsequently override such a State law
It concerns matters in the Concurrent List
President's assent makes the State law permanently immune from Parliamentary legislation
n1fbab16b296.x: Parliament may later override a State law even after it has received the President's assent.

n1caa09903f5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951)?
o: It is associated with the doctrine of pith and substance
The Prohibition Act was struck down because it touched imports
The Prohibition Act was upheld as a public-health measure
The Act only incidentally touched imports
n1caa09903f5.x: The Prohibition Act was upheld as a public-health measure even though it incidentally touched imports.

n741df9ff0b4.s:
Assertion (A): State of Bombay v. R.M.D.C. (1957) is associated with the doctrine of territorial nexus.
Reason (R): The case concerned the State's taxation of prize competitions conducted from outside the State.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n741df9ff0b4.x: Taxing prize competitions run from outside the State needed a nexus with the State, which is why the case is associated with territorial nexus.

n4c692c78602.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about separation of powers in India?
o: Kesavananda Bharati recognised separation of powers as a basic feature
Raj Narain held that the legislature could finally decide an election dispute
Raj Narain was connected with the challenge to the 39th Amendment
Deciding an election dispute is a judicial function
n4c692c78602.x: Raj Narain held the legislature cannot decide an election dispute because it is a judicial function.

n25172113540.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about parliamentary and presidential systems?
o: The parliamentary system rests on fusion of powers
The principal checks in the US system are checks and balances among the three organs
In India the President is the real executive and the Council of Ministers the nominal executive
In the USA the President is independent of Congress
n25172113540.x: In India the President is the nominal head and the Council of Ministers the real executive.

nfe31faa23f2.s: Which of the following was NOT a consideration behind the framers' choice of the parliamentary system?
o: Familiarity with parliamentary institutions under the Acts of 1919 and 1935
The need to accommodate India's diversity
The desire to avoid American-style executive–legislature conflict
Ambedkar's preference for stability over responsibility
nfe31faa23f2.x: Ambedkar preferred responsibility over stability, which is why the parliamentary system was chosen.

ne548d1308b7.s: Which Article bars discussion in Parliament on the conduct of a Supreme Court or High Court judge, except on a motion for removal?
ne548d1308b7.x: Article 121 bars it in Parliament and Article 211 in State Legislatures; Articles 122 and 212 stop courts inquiring into legislative proceedings for irregular procedure.

n53adccca0ad.s: The Governor's ordinance-making power is contained in Article:
n53adccca0ad.x: Article 213 covers State ordinances; Article 123 Union ordinances, Article 175 the Governor's addresses and Article 86 the President's addresses.

ne5fdfac8597.s: The 77th Constitutional Amendment (promotion quota) followed which judgment?
ne5fdfac8597.x: The 77th followed Indra Sawhney; the 24th followed Golaknath, the 26th Madhav Rao and the 1st Champakam Dorairajan.

n34b7b926707.s: Which Amendment placed Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule?
n34b7b926707.x: The 76th Amendment did so; after I.R. Coelho, such post-24 April 1973 entries can be reviewed if they damage the basic structure.

nd97e8568025.s: Parliament can override a judicial judgment by:
o: Changing the law or constitutional basis underlying it
A resolution of a joint sitting
nd97e8568025.x: Parliament can override a judgment only by changing its legal or constitutional basis, subject to the basic structure; a simple resolution cannot do it.

n5785de44a85.s: The 42nd Amendment's bar on judicial review was struck down in:
o: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975)
n5785de44a85.x: Minerva Mills struck down the bar; Raj Narain struck down the 39th Amendment's validation of the PM's election, and Golaknath predates the 42nd Amendment.

n772471a9fde.s: A no-confidence motion for removal of the government can be moved only in:
n772471a9fde.x: A no-confidence motion lies only in the Lok Sabha; Question Hour and Zero Hour give day-to-day watch over administration.

nd55f8a9e1fe.s: An ordinance, including one used to alter the legal basis of a judgment, can be issued when:
o: A National Emergency is in force
The legislature is not in session
nd55f8a9e1fe.x: An ordinance is issued when the legislature is not in session; it is subject to judicial review and must be laid before the House.

n81700615a23.s: Separation of powers in India is:
o: Implicit, not absolute, with overlapping functions creating checks and balances
Absolute, as in a pure presidential system
n81700615a23.x: India has no rigid separation; it is implicit, and overlapping functions create checks and balances.

ncda73232024.s: The Governor summons and prorogues the State Legislature under Article:
ncda73232024.x: The Governor acts under Article 174 (the President under Article 85); Article 175 is the Governor's address and messages. The gap between sessions cannot exceed six months.

n625e519b002.s: A law declared ultra vires by the courts in exercise of judicial review is:
n625e519b002.x: Judicial review covers laws and executive action, rests on Articles 13, 32 and 226, and an ultra vires law is void.

nd19c3aa3e7c.s: According to Montesquieu, the most effective means of protecting liberty is:
nd19c3aa3e7c.x: Montesquieu held that division of powers was the most effective way to protect liberty.

nindian-polity-8-15.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Elected members of the Lok Sabha – Vote in both the Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections
Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha – Vote in the Vice-Presidential but not the Presidential election
Members of State Legislative Councils – Vote in the Presidential election
Elected members of the Delhi and Puducherry Assemblies – Added to the Presidential Electoral College by the 70th Amendment
nindian-polity-8-15.x: Members of State Legislative Councils vote in neither the Presidential nor the Vice-Presidential election.

n3697af0c1ac.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the impeachment of the President under Article 61?
o: The initiating House may pass the charge by a simple majority
The other House investigates the charge
The President has the right to appear and be represented during the investigation
The other House must pass the charge by two-thirds of its total membership
n3697af0c1ac.x: Both Houses must pass the charge by a two-thirds majority of their total membership; a simple majority is not enough.
